title: When the Detention Sings
premise: Lena Thornbury, a debate champion who keeps her head down at home, discovers her late grandmother's recipe box contains coded instructions to a hidden student archive — decades of evidence against the school board's corrupt scholarship fund. When her best friend Priya's brother is framed for theft to cover the scheme, Lena must choose between staying invisible and exposing the truth, even if it destroys her friendship with the scholarship's beneficiaries. As the board closes in and the archive's location is threatened, Lena learns that winning an argument matters less than telling the truth. In the end she testifies publicly, loses some friendships but finds her voice, and honors her grandmother by rebuilding the archive as a student-run record of accountability.
about_author: Sebastian Dravenmoor is a former high-school debate coach who spent seven years watching teenagers find their voices in the most unlikely rooms. He writes from a converted garage in coastal Maine, where he keeps his own grandmother's recipe box on the windowsill.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. We meet Lena mid-debate-tournament victory, then watch her shrink the moment she gets home to her parents' cold silence over her grandmother's recent death. She wins arguments everywhere except her own kitchen. Emotional beat: the ache of being brilliant in public and invisible at home.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Sorting grandma's kitchen, Lena finds index cards that aren't recipes — numbered directions referencing 'the west wing shelf' and 'what they took.' The last card bears today's date from thirty years ago. Emotional beat: eerie curiosity; grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At school, Lena quietly checks the west wing shelf behind the trophy case and finds a hollowed-out yearbook containing microfilm and a ledger of names. She pockets it just as Vice-Principal Hargrove rounds the corner. Emotional beat: first taste of danger, thrilling and terrifying.

chapters.title: Priya Knows Everything
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Best friend Priya notices Lena acting strange; her loyalty runs deep, but her family depends on the Ashford Scholarship Lena's evidence implicates. She covers for Lena without asking questions. Emotional beat: love offered blindly, before either girl knows what it will cost.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Deciphering the ledger with debate-partner Marcus, Lena maps how the board funneled scholarship money to donors' children for decades. Her grandmother was the bookkeeper who kept copies. Emotional beat: righteous anger braided with fear — grandma knew, and stayed silent too.

chapters.title: Debate Club, After Hours
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus argues they should go public; Lena argues for caution, and wins — then hates winning. Their sparring doubles as forensics on the evidence. Emotional beat: the intoxication of using real skill for something that finally matters.

chapters.title: What They Took
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A card leads to a storage unit holding grandma's full testimony draft — never submitted because someone threatened her family. Lena realizes the threat was aimed at her mother. Emotional beat: the past reaching into the present; inherited silence.

chapters.title: The Frame
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's brother Devan is accused of stealing exam answer keys — a charge that smells engineered. Hargrove pushes expulsion fast. Priya begs Lena to help prove innocence, not knowing Lena already holds proof of a pattern. Emotional beat: desperation colliding with a secret too heavy to share.

chapters.title: Winning the Wrong Argument
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena defends Devan at a disciplinary hearing with flawless rhetoric — and wins him a suspension instead of expulsion, but not justice. Hargrove studies her afterward, too closely. Emotional beat: hollow victory; words can save or betray.

chapters.title: Hargrove's Offer
chapters.summary: Hargrove's POV. The vice-principal, himself compromised, offers Lena a college recommendation and her family's protection if she returns what she took. He reveals he knows about the recipe box. Emotional beat: corruption wearing a reasonable face; temptation dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: Tell Me the Truth
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers the ledger in Lena's locker while returning a borrowed jacket. Confrontation: why did you hide this when my brother needed it? Emotional beat: the friendship cracks along the fault line between loyalty and truth.

chapters.title: Silence Is Also a Choice
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena confronts her mother about grandma's silence and learns mom suspected everything and chose safety. The argument Lena could never win at home finally happens — and nobody wins it. Emotional beat: generational cowardice named out loud, painfully.

chapters.title: The West Wing Shelf
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The trio reconvenes: archive, ledger, testimony. They plan to copy everything and distribute it before the board can purge records at semester's end. Emotional beat: fragile alliance rebuilt on shared stakes rather than comfort.

chapters.title: Copy Machine at Midnight
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A tense break-in to duplicate documents in the admin building; Priya stands lookout, hands shaking, choosing the friendship over the scholarship. They nearly get caught by a janitor who turns out to be grandma's old ally. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into solidarity.

chapters.title: The Janitor's Testimony
chapters.summary: New character Mr. Okafor's POV. The janitor reveals he witnessed the original cover-up and kept one piece of evidence hidden for thirty years, waiting for someone brave enough to ask. Emotional beat: hope arriving from the least expected quarter; courage is contagious.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The board retaliates: Devan's suspension becomes expulsion, Marcus's captaincy is revoked, and anonymous threats appear in Lena's locker. Someone inside their circle talked — or was flipped. Emotional beat: siege mentality; trust under pressure.

chapters.title: Which Side Are You On
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Suspicion poisons the trio until they trace the leak to a well-meaning classmate coerced by Hargrove. Instead of exiling them, Lena recruits them. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy; power over people versus power with people.

chapters.title: The Motion to Proceed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Using debate-champion craft, Lena engineers a public forum — a mock trial of the scholarship program — where the evidence must be heard on the record with press invited. Emotional beat: turning the enemy's rules into a weapon; the calm before the storm.

chapters.title: When the Detention Sings
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The forum erupts: Hargrove produces a forged letter implicating grandma; Lena counters with the microfilm, the janitor's testimony, and her mother standing up to corroborate. Students chant from the back rows. Emotional beat: the climax — truth spoken aloud, costly and unstoppable.

chapters.title: Costs and Settlements
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Fallout: Hargrove resigns, the state audits the fund, Devan is reinstated — but two friendships don't survive, and Lena's name is mud among the scholarship families. Emotional beat: victory that grieves; justice is not free.

chapters.title: The Empty Shelf
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, having lost her scholarship prospects anyway, helps Lena formally donate the archive to the school library as a permanent student-run accountability record. An uneasy truce becomes honest conversation. Emotional beat: reconciliation without erasure; the friendship remade truer.

chapters.title: Grades Up, Head High
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Months later, Lena competes in the state final and deliberately loses a round rather than argue a position she doesn't believe — her first honest defeat. At home, dinner conversations have changed. The recipe box sits open on her desk, now holding new cards. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; a voice found and kept.
